summary.headline: robots.txt clearly intends a symmetric, blanket block of every major AI company's crawlers, but names a retired Anthropic token ('Claude-Web') and a misspelled Perplexity token ('PerplexityUser', missing the hyphen) instead of each company's current, correctly-spelled agent names -- so Anthropic's and Perplexity's actual current crawlers are not disallowed at all — critical severity, Replace 'Claude-Web' with 'Claude-User' and 'Claude-SearchBot', and correct 'PerplexityUser' to 'Perplexity-User', matching the rest of the file's already-correct entries (e.g. 'PerplexityBot').

findings.title: robots.txt clearly intends a symmetric, blanket block of every major AI company's crawlers, but names a retired Anthropic token ('Claude-Web') and a misspelled Perplexity token ('PerplexityUser', missing the hyphen) instead of each company's current, correctly-spelled agent names -- so Anthropic's and Perplexity's actual current crawlers are not disallowed at all
findings.evidence: robots.txt disallows GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, CCBot, OAI-SearchBot, Google-Extended, anthropic-ai, Applebot-Extended, Bytespider, Claude-Web, cohere-ai, Diffbot, FacebookBot, omgili, omgilibot, PerplexityBot and PerplexityUser -- a comprehensive, deliberate, symmetric list clearly intended to block training and retrieval agents alike from every major operator, unlike the more common asymmetric patterns found elsewhere. But 'Claude-Web' is a retired Anthropic token; the current tokens are 'Claude-User' (live user-request fetches) and 'Claude-SearchBot' (Claude's search indexing), neither of which appears anywhere in the file. Verified directly with this project's own robots.txt parser against a real article path: Claude-User and Claude-SearchBot both resolve 'allowed' (falling through to the wildcard group, which disallows only specific paths, not the whole site), while the file's own intent is obviously to block them the same as every other operator's agents. The same pattern repeats for Perplexity: 'PerplexityUser' (no hyphen) is not a documented Perplexity token -- the real one is 'Perplexity-User' -- and it likewise resolves 'allowed'. 'PerplexityBot' is spelled correctly and is genuinely disallowed, showing the intent was there; the execution missed two of the four Anthropic/Perplexity tokens that needed it.

reproduction.observed: User-agent: Claude-Web / Disallow: / and User-agent: PerplexityUser / Disallow: / are present; 'Claude-User', 'Claude-SearchBot' and 'Perplexity-User' (the current, correctly-spelled tokens) do not appear anywhere in the file and resolve 'allowed' via the wildcard group
reproduction.expected: The current, correctly-spelled tokens for every operator already named in the file, so the file's own clearly stated intent (block every major AI crawler) is actually achieved

suggested_action.summary: Replace 'Claude-Web' with 'Claude-User' and 'Claude-SearchBot', and correct 'PerplexityUser' to 'Perplexity-User', matching the rest of the file's already-correct entries (e.g. 'PerplexityBot').
suggested_action.mechanism: This is a two-line typo/staleness fix, not a policy decision -- the file already states the intended policy correctly for every other operator (OpenAI's three tokens, Google's, Meta's, Common Crawl's, Cohere's, ByteDance's are all current and correct). Anthropic's Claude and Perplexity's answer engine can very likely still fetch and cite this content live today, silently contradicting a policy the site otherwise enforces comprehensively.
steps: Replace the 'Claude-Web' entry with 'Claude-User' and add 'Claude-SearchBot' as a separate entry, both with Disallow: /.
Re-verify all agent tokens against each operator's current published documentation, since this is exactly the kind of drift that recurs as operators rename or add agents.
suggested_action.verification: Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot and Perplexity-User all resolve 'disallowed' against the same path GPTBot and PerplexityBot already do.

not_assessed.check: Structured data, answerability, freshness/corroboration, and engagement on article pages
not_assessed.reason: This run focused entirely on precisely verifying one high-confidence robots.txt token-staleness finding rather than sampling article content.
not_assessed.impact: Cannot state whether NPR's article markup, prose quality, or on-site experience have defects; a genuine scope limit of this run, not a claim about the site either way.
